correctness.rationale: Fourier characters diagonalize both quadratic difference forms. If \(r(k)\) coordinates of a frequency are odd, the long-difference energy is \(4r(k)/n\), while averaging over independent signs gives sign energy \(2(1-\prod_j\cos(\pi k_j/m))\). For \(c=\cos(\pi/m)\), any positive cosine product is at most \(c^{r(k)}\), and \(r/(1-c^r)\) is increasing in positive \(r\); nonpositive products give no larger ratio. Hence the maximum is at \(k=(1,\ldots,1)\) and equals \(2/(1-c^n)\). The conjugate-pair real span attains the same ratio, so the complex Fourier computation is valid over real scalars. Wang's exact quotient duality then transfers this to the adjoint lifting constant; normalization gives the displayed \(L_{n,m}\), and the Taylor expansion of \(\log\cos(\pi/m)\) gives the sharp-scale limit. Independent enumeration for small \(n\) and even \(m\), including \(m=2\), reproduced the maximizing frequency and formula.
